image_description: A grey whale surfacing in calm, grey ocean waters. The whale's head and upper back are visible above the waterline, displaying a prominent spout of mist from its blowholes. The skin appears dark grey with lighter mottling consistent with barnacle patches. No dorsal fin is visible, only the curve of the back leading into the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is consistent with a grey whale, showing a blunt, arched rostrum. A distinct spout indicates the presence of blowholes, although the holes themselves are partially obscured by the spray and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin exhibits the characteristic mottled grey coloration with lighter, irregular patches typical of cyamid and barnacle infestations found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the absence of a dorsal fin is consistent with the visible portion, the 'multiple dorsal knuckles' are located further down the back which is submerged or out of frame, making this specific feature untestable in this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior section of the whale is visible; the full spindle shape and total proportions cannot be verified as the rear body and tail are submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible back area shows the correct mottled texture and coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whale's mouth is closed and underwater; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external surfacing shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located on the underside/lateral aspects of the body and are completely submerged/occluded in this image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are at the posterior end of the animal and are not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin surface appears textured and uneven, consistent with the rough texture and callosities described in the taxonomy.
